subject: ACME POC: integration plan, success criteria, and kickoff
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Jane Doe <jane.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 15:10:00 -0800
Subject: ACME POC: integration plan, success criteria, and kickoff

Hi Jane -

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have aligned expectations for the POC/trial: 

Summary of goals (per our call):
- Validate retrieval-and-generation flow for customer support triage (latency < 400ms median for 512-token prompts)
- Maintain answer accuracy > 85% on your eval set (we'll need the eval prompts)
- Confirm streaming and tool-calling reliability for agent assist integrations

Proposed success criteria (please confirm):
1) Latency: median end-to-end token latency < 400ms under 10 RPS synthetic load
2) Quality: >= 85% accuracy on your labeled 200-item eval set
3) Stability: no more than 1% error rate over a 3-hour soak test

POC timeline (suggested):
- Week 0: kickoff + sandbox credentials exchanged (owner: Marissa)
- Week 1: integration + basic SDK test (owner: Dev)
- Week 2: run eval set, tune prompts, enable streaming/tool calling tests (owner: ACME eng + Dev)
- Week 3: soak, measurement, and success criteria review (owner: Rishi + ACME PO)

Integration notes / initial asks for your engineering team:
- We support our Python/Node SDKs; you can also call the REST routes directly.
- Streaming (chunked responses) is enabled via /v1/generate/stream and WebSocket options - useful for your agent UI.
- Tool calling: we expose a tool-call API and a structured JSON response mode if you want deterministic tool invocations.

Attachments I'm including: POC_Mutual_Action_Plan.pdf (milestones/owners) and Redwood_API_Specs.md (endpoints + examples). Dev, I've cc'd you for the technical details.

Next steps: can you confirm the success criteria above and share the technical contact and sandbox credentials? If that looks good I'll schedule a 30-minute kickoff for next Wed morning.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cell: (415) 555-0142

From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 13:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: ACME POC: integration plan, success criteria, and kickoff

Tom - quick technical plan and what we need from ACME to get the SDK + streaming + tool-calling tests running this week. Pasting the high-level steps below and attaching a small SDK example (SDK_example.py) and the API spec (Redwood_API_Specs.md).

High-level integration steps:
1) Sandbox creds + test corpus access (ACME action)
2) Install SDK (pip install redwood-sdk) or hit REST endpoints directly
   - SDK usage (python):
     from redwood import RedwoodClient
     client = RedwoodClient(api_key="<SANDBOX_KEY>")
     with client.generate_stream(model="redwood/fast-1", prompt=prompt) as stream:
         for chunk in stream:
             print(chunk.text, end="")

3) API routes you'll use: /v1/generate (sync), /v1/generate/stream (streaming), /v1/tools/call (tool invocation webhook pattern)
4) For tool calling, we support structured responses: response.type = "tool_call" and a tool payload with name/args. We can also proxy webhooks if you want the tool executed by your infra.
5) Test plan: run 50 synthetic requests with streaming enabled and compare latency distribution; run eval set and return predictions csv.

Questions / asks from ACME:
- Can you provide a small set of representative prompts and a single test user account for end-to-end checks?
- Do you prefer the SDK or direct REST for the initial integration (we can provide both samples)?

I'll be online during the kickoff to pair on auth and initial SDK run.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer
dev.patel@redwood.com
